policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Qere וְיֹדְעֵי is a construct participle (HC/Vqrmpc), 'and they that know [thy testimonies]'; ketiv וידעו is a finite consecutive perfect (HC/Vqq3cp), 'and they shall know'. ASV main text reads 'And they shall know thy testimonies' — a finite clause — and the mapped note on this verse, 'Another reading is, Even they that know.', gives the participial qere as the alternative. The finite verb plus the note distinguish the ketiv.

Qere לִדְבָרְךָ is singular (HR/Ncmsc/Sp2ms); ketiv לדבריך is plural (HR/Ncmpc/Sp2ms). ASV reads 'I hoped in thy words' — plural — where ASV renders grammatical number of דָּבָר reliably (compare the singular 'thy word' elsewhere in this psalm). The plural distinguishes the ketiv. No note is mapped to the word.

Qere וּמִדְּבָרְךָ is singular (HC/R/Ncmsc/Sp2ms); ketiv ומדבריך is plural (HC/R/Ncmpc/Sp2ms). ASV reads 'But my heart standeth in awe of thy words' — plural — the same number choice ASV makes at 119:147 for this ketiv/qere pair. The plural distinguishes the ketiv. No note is mapped to the word.
